questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 69 + 2485 × 5 – 912 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?
69 + 2485 × 5 – 912 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.solution:
69 + 2485 × 5 – 912 ÷ 2  ⇒ 69 - 2485 ÷ 5 + 912 × 2 

⇒ 69 - 2485 ÷ 5 + 912 × 2  ⇒ 69 - 497 + 912 × 2  ⇒ 69 + 1824 - 497  ⇒ 1893 - 497  ⇒ 1396

questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
X + Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’,
X − Y means ‘X is the wife of Y’,
X × Y means ‘X is the mother of Y’,
X ÷ Y means ‘X is the father of Y’.
Based on the above, how is H related to L if ‘H × I − J ÷ K + L’?
questions.solution: Thus, H is L's mother’s mother or maternal grandmother.

questions.question: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some shirts are pants. All pants are jackets. All jackets are trousers. Conclusions: I. Some trousers are shirts. II. All jackets are shirts.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be
true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically
follows/follow from the statements.
Statements:
Some shirts are pants.
All pants are jackets.
All jackets are trousers.
Conclusions:
I. Some trousers are shirts.
II. All jackets are shirts.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
options.html: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
options.html: Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some trousers are shirts → Follow (As some shirts are pants, all pants are jackets and all jackets are trousers. As whole pants comes in jackets and whole jacket comes in trousers and some part of pants is common with shirts, therefore it is true.)

II. All jackets are shirts → Does not follow (As some shirts are pants and all pants are jackets. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.
